taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: stems 30 cm to 1 m tall, 1.5 m at most.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: rays 3 cm to 7.5 cm long, each ending in an umbellet: a compound umbel, compact in fruit (genus, p. 227).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves 5 cm to 20 cm long.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: leaves finely cut into linear or lanceolate segments 2 mm to 12 mm long; the genus has pinnately decompound leaves (p. 227).

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 227, Daucus: pinnately decompound leaves.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 216, Daucus, in the key to genera: leaves three or four times pinnately cut; drawn three times divided, the last division the lobes of each pinnule.

traits.pinnae.note: Fifteen primary divisions, seven pairs and a terminal one (6 to 9 pairs in the photos), set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.pinnules.note: Seven pinnules to each primary division, each pinna itself ovate-deltoid, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaflets.note: Five lobes to each pinnule (3 to 7 in the photos), set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Each division ending in one, set by hand from the photos: Abrams (1951 p. 228) does not say.

traits.division_planes.note: Mostly flat sprays, each pinna close to one plane, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: linear or lanceolate last segments.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: linear or lanceolate segments 2 mm to 12 mm long.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Lobes 1 mm to 1.5 mm wide, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 216, Daucus, in the key to genera: leaves more or less hairy; the genus is pubescent (p. 227).

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: flowers white, yellow or pinkish, the umbel's central flower purple or pink; drawn white, sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: fruit ovoid, 3 mm to 4 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: introduced from Europe and well established in western Washington and Oregon, flowering May to September.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: biennial from a slender spindle-shaped taproot.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 228, Daucus carota: rays 3 cm to 7.5 cm long, white flowers. Drawn as a flat-topped umbel of umbellets of 20 small white flowers; the purple central flower is not drawn.

generator.params.note: Cow parsnip's values, changed by hand for wild carrot: a rosette of finely divided basal leaves and one stem with smaller leaves, ending in a white compound umbel (Abrams 1951 p. 228). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.6 m tall in its second (flowering) year in the open, the middle of the model's 0.3-1 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1951 pp. 227-228): mid-green, hairy, finely divided leaves; green hairy stems; white flowers. The leaves narrowly triangular, the pinnae longest near the foot and narrowing evenly to a small tip (largest 0.1, lowest 0.3), from iNaturalist photos (observations 111603572, 200104113, 288552142, 329573306, 357823924, 363817289, 370479050, 44929874, 72299212).
